proof_summary: For the counterexample $n=800{,}322{,}180$, monotonicity and $\binom{33}{16}=1{,}166{,}803{,}110>n$ force $0\le c\le d\le15$. For each of these finitely many pairs, $n-\binom{2c+1}{c}-\binom{2d+1}{d}$ has a prime congruent to $3\pmod4$ to an odd exponent, so it cannot be a sum of two squares.
